mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers the cost of capital, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.5% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential investment (RSAFS) and new housing starts (HOUST) indicates a weakening housing market, which reduces consumer wealth and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index 2017=100), manufacturing sector weakness signals reduced corporate capacity utilization and lower future earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 150,000 thousand persons signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 150,000, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% annually, it signals rising inflation expectations that prompt central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (annualized), or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% signals a central bank's attempt to stimulate the economy amid persistent inflation, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL > 2.0%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%) and high job growth (PAYEMS > 200,000), the labor market is overheating, which leads to wage pressures and potential central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS > 200,000, or the Rank IC for the joint condition is below 0.03.
